He mentions four matters: creation (al-khalq), proportioning (al-taswiyah), determining (al-taqdir), and guidance (al-hidayah).

Guidance is teaching. So He mentioned that He is the One who created and taught, just as He mentioned a similar thing at the beginning of the surah He sent down to His Messenger ﷺ. That has already been discussed.

God, the Exalted, said, relating the words of His enemy Pharaoh, that he said to Musa: ﴿"Who then is the Lord of you two, O Musa?" He said: "Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it."﴾

This level is the earliest of the levels of guidance and the most general.

In *Shifa' al-'Alil* he said:

He, glory be to Him, mentioned four general matters: creation, proportioning, determining, and guidance. He made proportioning part of the completeness of creation, and guidance part of the completeness of determining.

ʿAtaʾ said: "He created and proportioned it in the best form He created it." Its evidence is His saying: ﴿He who made beautiful everything He created﴾. So the beauty of His creation includes its proportioning, and the harmony of His creation and its parts, such that no disparity arose among them that would disturb the harmony and balance. Thus creation is bringing into existence, and proportioning is perfecting it and making its creation beautiful.

Al-Kalbi said: "He created every living being and gathered its creation and proportioned it with two hands, two eyes, and two feet."

Muqatil said: "He created for every beast what suits it of creation."

Abu Ishaq said: "He created man upright."

This is an example, for creation and proportioning encompass man and others. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾, and He said: ﴿So He proportioned them as seven heavens﴾. So proportioning encompasses all His creatures: ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disparity﴾. Whatever disparity and lack of proportion exists goes back to not giving the created thing proportioning, for proportioning is an existential matter related to effecting and originating. What lacks it lacks it because the Creator did not will proportioning for it, and that is a privative matter, for which the absence of origination and effecting suffices.

So reflect on this, for it will remove from you the difficulty in His saying: ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disparity﴾.

Disparity occurs because the will of proportioning is absent, just as ignorance, deafness, blindness, muteness, and dumbness are sufficiently explained by the absence of the will to create and bring them into existence. The full treatment of this will come, God willing, in the chapter on the entry of evil into divine decree, regarding the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "And evil is not attributed to You."

The point is that every creature has been proportioned by its Creator, glory be to Him, in the rank of its creation, even if it lacks proportioning in another respect, since it was not created for that.

(Section)

As for determining and guidance, Muqatil said: "He determined the creation of the male and the female, and guided the male to the female, how he comes to her."

Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Kalbi, and likewise ʿAtaʾ said: "He determined the offspring as He willed, then guided the male to the female."

The one who chose this view was the author of *al-Nazm*, who said: "The meaning of guided is guiding the male to coming to the female, how he comes to her."

Because the mating of male animals with their females varies according to the differences in forms, creation, and states, if God, the Exalted, had not disposed each male to know how to come to a female of its kind, it would not have been guided to that.

Muqatil also said: "He guided it to its livelihood and pasture."

Al-Suddi said: "He determined the duration of the fetus in the womb, then guided it to come out."

Mujahid said: "He guided man to the path of good and evil, and happiness and wretchedness."

Al-Farraʾ said: "The determining is 'then guided,' and 'and led astray,' so one was mentioned and the other was omitted."

I say: The verse is more general than all of this, and the weakest of the views on it is the view of al-Farraʾ, since what is meant here is the general guidance to the welfare of animals in their livelihood, not the guidance of faith and the leading astray by His will.

This is like His saying: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided﴾.

So giving creation is bringing it into existence externally, and guidance is teaching and indicating the way of its survival and what preserves and sustains it.

As for what Mujahid mentioned, it is an example from him, not an exact explanation of the verse, for the verse includes the guidance of all animals, speaking and dumb, birds and beasts, the eloquent and the mute.

Likewise the view of the one who said it is the guiding of the male to coming to the female is also an example, and it is one individual instance of the guidance which none can count except God.

Likewise the view of the one who said He guided it to pasture, for that is part of guidance. Guidance includes the guidance to seize the breast when it emerges from its mother's womb, the guidance to recognize its mother over others so that it follows her wherever she goes, and the guidance to aim at what benefits it in pasture and avoid what harms it.

Also the guidance of birds, beasts, and animals to wonderful acts that man cannot do, such as the guidance of the bee to follow the paths in which its pastures lie, despite their diversity, and then its return to its hives from trees, mountains, and what the children of Adam plant.

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾. This is in truth a proof against them, for the Prophet carried out this command and said: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High," and "Glory be to my Lord the Great." Had the matter been as they claimed, he would have said "Glory be to the name of my Lord the Great." Moreover, none of the community may say "I worshipped the name of my Lord," or "I prostrated to the name of my Lord," or "I bowed to the name of my Lord," or "by the name of my Lord, have mercy on me." This shows that things are connected to the named, not to the name.

As for the answer about the connection of the remembrance and glorification commanded with the name, it has been said that glorifying and exalting, when due to the one glorified, extend to what is from his cause and connected to him, as one says "peace be upon ..." and "the exalted gate" and "the noble assembly" and the like. But this answer is not satisfactory for two reasons. The first is that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not understand this meaning, but said "Glory be to my Lord," so he did not turn to what you mentioned. The second is that it would require applying to the name takbir, tahmid, tahlil, and all that is applied to the named, so one would say "praise is for the name of God" and "there is no god but the name of God" and the like. No one has said this. Rather, the correct answer is that true remembrance has its seat in the heart, for it is the opposite of forgetfulness, and glorification is a kind of remembrance. So if remembrance and glorification are mentioned without qualification, nothing is understood from them except that, rather than uttering with the tongue. God, the Exalted, desired from His servants both together, and He did not accept faith or the establishment of Islam except by their conjunction and union. So the meaning of the two verses becomes: glorify your Lord with your heart and tongue, and remember your Lord with your heart and tongue. The name was inserted to draw attention to this meaning, so that glorification and remembrance are not devoid of utterance by the tongue, for the object of the remembrance of the heart is the named, indicated by the name, not anything else. And the remembrance by the tongue has as its object the utterance together with what it signifies, for the utterance is not intended for itself, so no one supposes that the utterance is what is glorified apart from the meaning it indicates.

My shaykh Abu al-ʿAbbas Ibn Taymiyyah, may God sanctify his soul, expressed this meaning in a subtle and concise phrase. He said: "The meaning is: glorify, speaking the name of your Lord," that is, pronouncing it. Likewise: ﴿What you worship besides Him are only names you have named﴾, and ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord﴾: the meaning is "glorify your Lord, mentioning His name." This benefit is worth a journey, but only for one who knows its value. So praise be to God, the Bestower, by His grace, and we ask Him to complete His favor.

Third argument: they said, God, the Exalted, said: ﴿What you worship besides Him are only names you have named﴾, and they only worshipped the named things.

The answer: as you said, they only worshipped the named things, but that is because they gave them false names, such as al-Lat and al-ʿUzza, which are merely false, baseless names with no named reality in truth. They named them gods and worshipped them because they believed in the reality of their divinity, yet they have no divinity except the mere names, not the reality of the named. So they worshipped only names without realities for their named objects. This is like one who names onion skins "meat" and eats them; it is said: "You ate nothing of the meat but its name, not its named reality." Or like one who names dirt "bread" and eats it; it is said: "You ate nothing but the name of bread." Indeed, this negation is more forceful regarding their gods, for there is no reality of divinity for them in any respect, and "what is the wisdom" in them is nothing but the name. So reflect on this noble benefit in His speech, the Exalted.

If it is said: what is the point of the particle bi (with) in His saying: ﴿So glorify with the name of your Lord, the Great﴾, while it does not occur in His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾?

It is answered: tasbih (glorification) may be intended as mere exaltation and pure remembrance with no other meaning, and it may be intended together with prayer, which is remembrance and exaltation together with action. For this reason prayer is called tasbih. So when pure tasbih is intended, there is no sense in the bi, for it is not transitive with a prepositional particle; you do not say "I glorified with God." But when you intend it together with the act, which is prayer, you add the bi to indicate that intended meaning, as if you said: "glorify, beginning with the name of your Lord" or "speaking the name of your Lord," just as you say "pray, beginning" or "speaking His name." For this secret, and God knows best, the lam was added in His saying: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God﴾.

The intended tasbih here is that which is prostration, submission, and obedience. In no place did He say "glorify God" with what is in the heavens and the earth, as He said: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15].

Reflect on His saying: ﴿Indeed those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206].

How He said "and they glorify Him" when He had mentioned prostration by His particular name. So the tasbih became their remembrance of Him and their declaring Him free of imperfection.

They named them gods and worshipped them because they believed in the reality of their divinity, yet they have no divinity except the mere names, not the reality of the named. So they worshipped only names without realities for their named objects. This is like one who names onion skins "meat" and eats them; it is said: "You ate nothing of the meat but its name, not its named reality." Or like one who names dirt "bread" and eats it; it is said: "You ate nothing but the name of bread." Indeed, this negation is more forceful regarding their gods, for there is no reality of divinity for them in any respect, and "what is the wisdom" in them is nothing but the name. So reflect on this noble benefit in His speech, the Exalted.

If it is said: what is the point of the particle bi (with) in His saying: ﴿So glorify with the name of your Lord, the Great﴾, while it does not occur in His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾?

It is answered: tasbih (glorification) may be intended as mere exaltation and pure remembrance with no other meaning, and it may be intended together with prayer, which is remembrance and exaltation together with action. For this reason prayer is called tasbih. So when pure tasbih is intended, there is no sense in the bi, for it is not transitive with a prepositional particle; you do not say "I glorified with God." But when you intend it together with the act, which is prayer, you add the bi to indicate that intended meaning, as if you said: "glorify, beginning with the name of your Lord" or "speaking the name of your Lord," just as you say "pray, beginning" or "speaking His name." For this secret, and God knows best, the lam was added in His saying: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God﴾.

The intended tasbih here is that which is prostration, submission, and obedience. In no place did He say "glorify God" with what is in the heavens and the earth, as He said: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15].

Reflect on His saying: ﴿Indeed those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206].

How He said "and they glorify Him" when He had mentioned prostration by His particular name. So the tasbih became their remembrance of Him and their declaring Him free of imperfection.

For he who does not believe in the Hereafter, the most he will say is: "These are a people whom time has afflicted, just as it has afflicted others, and time has always contained both misery and happiness."

As for one who believes in the Hereafter and fears it, he is the one who benefits from the signs and the admonitions.

Indeed, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Since in this world he did not live the true, beneficial life for which he was created, but his life was of the kind of the life of beasts, and he was not dead and devoid of perception, his life in the Hereafter is likewise.

The purpose of life is the attainment of that which one benefits from and takes pleasure in, and the living necessarily has either pleasure or pain. So when he does not attain pleasure, he does not attain the purpose of life, like one who is alive in this world but has grave illnesses that stand between him and enjoying what the healthy enjoy. He chooses death and wishes for it, but it is not granted to him; so he is neither among the living nor among the dead.

Having understood this, evil is a necessary consequence of this life, and its absence is an evil. Yet it is not a thing, such that it would be created, and God is the Creator of all things.

So when He withholds this life from a servant, its withholding is good in relation to Him, glorified is He, though it is an evil in relation to the servant, due to the loss of what he would take pleasure and delight in. Evil deeds are of the nature of the soul, and it was not granted this life, which would have stood between it and them.

Thus all evil is from the soul, and all good is from God, and all of it is by His decree, His destiny, and His wisdom. And success is from God.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 87, verses 14–17:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, you prefer the worldly life﴾

The purpose is to establish this sentence, not to turn away from His saying: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾.

(Benefit)

Desire for the Hereafter is not complete except through asceticism (zuhd) in this world, and asceticism in this world is not upright except after two sound considerations:

The first is a consideration of this world, its swift passing, its perishing and its dissolution, its deficiency and its baseness, the pain of competing for it and of greed for it, and what there is in that of anguish, turbulence and sorrows.

The last of that is its ending and cessation, together with the regret and grief that follow it.

So the one who seeks it is never free of worry before attaining it, of anxiety while holding it, and of grief and sorrow after losing it. This is the first of the two considerations.

The second consideration: a consideration of the Hereafter, its approach and its coming, which is certain, its permanence and its enduring, the nobility of what is in it of goods and joys, and the difference between it and what is here. It is the perfection of God, glorified is He: ﴿And the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾.

It consists of complete, enduring goods, whereas this is a deficient, cut-off, dissolving illusion. When both of these considerations are complete for him, he prefers what reason requires him to prefer and renounces what calls for renunciation. Every person is naturally disposed not to abandon immediate benefit and present pleasure for a deferred benefit and an absent, awaited pleasure, until it becomes clear to him that the deferred is superior to the immediate and his desire for the higher and more excellent grows strong. So when one prefers the perishing and deficient, that is either because the superiority has not become clear to him, or because he has no desire for the more excellent.

Each of the two matters indicates weakness of faith and weakness of intellect and insight. For the one who desires the world, is greedy for it and prefers it, either he believes that what is there is more noble, more excellent and more lasting, or he does not believe that. If he does not believe it, he is utterly devoid of faith; and if he believes it but does not prefer it, he is corrupt of intellect and bad in choosing for himself. This is a clear, necessary division, and the servant cannot escape one of its two parts. Therefore, preferring the world over the Hereafter arises either from corruption in faith or from corruption in intellect.

How often do both of these occur! For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions cast the world behind their backs, turned their hearts away from it, rejected it, did not grow attached to it, did not shun it out of aversion, did not incline towards it, and regarded it as a prison, not a paradise. They renounced it in the true sense of renunciation. Had they wished for it, they would have obtained from it every beloved thing and reached every desired thing. The keys to its treasures were offered to him, and he refused them; they overflowed upon his companions, and they preferred the Hereafter and did not sell their share of it for the world. They knew that it is a crossing and a passageway, not an abode of residence and settlement, a house of passing, not a house of joy, a summer cloud that dissipates in a little while, and a phantom of a dream: it had not completed its visit before it announced departure. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"What have I to do with the world? I am only like a rider who rested in the shade of a tree, then went on and left it."

And he said: "The likeness of this world compared with the Hereafter is only like one of you dipping his finger into the sea; let him see what it returns with."

And its Creator, glorified is He, said: ﴿The likeness of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, of which men and livestock eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it a harvested field as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus We detail the signs for a people who reflect. And God calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

So He informed about the baseness of this world and renounced it, and He informed about the Abode of Peace and called to it.

(Section)

Exertion in obedience is mixed with beauty and produces delight and ease. So when it becomes heavy upon the soul, reflect on the cessation of its toil and the lasting of its beauty, its delight and its joy, weigh the two, and prefer the weightier over the lighter.

This requires knowledge of causes and their consequences, and an intellect by which one chooses what is first and most beneficial for oneself. So whoever fulfils his share of intellect and knowledge and chooses the better and prefers it, and whoever diminishes his share of them, or of one of them, chooses the opposite.

Whoever reflects on this world and the Hereafter knows that he cannot attain either of them except with hardship; so let him bear the hardship for the sake of the better and more lasting of the two.
